title: Beyond Highlights: How Gujarat Titans Could Build an Interactive Fan Experience
dek: Highlights show a few moments. An interactive Gujarat Titans experience could let fans explore every ball, and the data to power it largely exists already.
excerpt: Gujarat Titans' matches are recorded ball by ball, and most deliveries carry tags for the shot, the scoring zone and the length. That is the raw material for fan experiences that go far beyond highlights.

sections.heading: From Highlights to Exploration
body: Highlights packages choose the moments for fans. An interactive experience would let fans choose: every boundary a favourite batter hit through cover, every yorker at the death in a final.
The CricField warehouse already holds {{ev:bh-n}} deliveries from {{ev:bh-m}} Gujarat Titans matches.

sections.heading: What Each Ball Carries
body: {{ev:bh-shot}} of those deliveries carry the shot played, {{ev:bh-zone}} the scoring zone and {{ev:bh-len}} the length. Only {{ev:bh-spd}} carry a speed.
The chart shows coverage for each field.

sections.heading: Proposal: What Fans Could Do
body: Proposal: wagon wheels filtered by bowler type and phase, a "replay the chase" mode that steps through each ball with the win-probability model from this series, and personal stat cards for any player.

sections.heading: Rights and Gaps
body: Video rights sit with the broadcaster and the league, so an interactive product would pair data with licensed clips or use data visuals alone. Speed data is too sparse for pace-based features.
Commentary tags are human-entered, so fan-facing tools should show coverage honestly.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: The Data Is Ready Before the Product
body: For Gujarat Titans, the ball-by-ball data needed for an interactive fan experience is largely in place.
The constraint is rights and design, not data.
